items.cite: Richard Osborne, *Rossini: His Life and Works*, 2nd ed. (Oxford University Press, 2007).
items.note: What happened during the decades after William Tell, and how do the serious operas fit beside the comedies? Osborne treats the whole career and its music.

items.cite: Emanuele Senici, ed., *The Cambridge Companion to Rossini* (Cambridge University Press, 2004).
items.note: How were these operas assembled for particular theatres and singers? Chapters on librettos, compositional methods, ornamentation, staging and editing answer different parts of that question.

items.cite: Philip Gossett, *Divas and Scholars: Performing Italian Opera* (University of Chicago Press, 2006).
items.note: Which version should be performed, what should be cut, and how much may a singer ornament? Gossett explains the editorial decisions that change a Rossini evening.

items.cite: Fausto Petrella, ‘Spazio artistico e umorismo in musica. Il comico musicale e i suoi rapporti con il Witz’, *De Musica* 7 (2003).
items.note: How can strictly organised singing sound like collective confusion? Section VIII examines ensembles from The Barber of Seville, La Cenerentola and L’italiana in Algeri. In Italian.
